Compute or Attach Confidence Intervals for an amerasfit Object

confint.Rd

Compute confidence or credible intervals for the parameters of a fitted amerasfit object. confint() returns standalone interval bounds. add_confint() attaches bounds and any available diagnostics to a copy of the fitted object for inclusion in summary() output, and records confidence-interval timing.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'amerasfit'
confint(object, parm="dose", level=0.95,
        type=c("proflik","percentile"), maxit.profCI=100,
        tol.profCI=1e-6, data=NULL, ...)

add_confint(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'amerasfit'
add_confint(object, parm="dose", level=0.95,
        type=c("proflik","percentile"), maxit.profCI=100,
        tol.profCI=1e-6, data=NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model object of class amerasfit, as returned by ameras.

parm

Either "dose" to compute profile likelihood intervals for dose-related parameters only, "all" for all parameters, or a character vector of parameter names. Only used when type = "proflik". Defaults to "dose" because profile likelihood intervals can be computationally intensive.

level

Confidence level, as a single number between zero and one. Defaults to 0.95.

type

Interval type. For RC, ERC, and MCML, use "wald.orig", "wald.transformed", or "proflik". For FMA and BMA, use "percentile" or "hpd". When both groups of methods are present, supply one type for each group.

maxit.profCI

Maximum number of root-finding iterations per profile likelihood bound. Defaults to 100. This does not control the separate bracketing search or the nuisance-parameter optimizer.

tol.profCI

Root-finding tolerance on the internal optimizer parameter scale. Defaults to 1e-6. Larger values can reduce computation time, particularly for ERC and MCML, but may produce inaccurate bounds. A bound is returned as NA with a warning if root finding warns or its p-value differs from 1 - level by more than 0.005, even when a larger tolerance is explicitly requested.

data

Original fitting data. Required for profile likelihood intervals when the model was fitted with keep.data = FALSE.

...

Additional arguments, currently unused.

Value

confint()

For an object containing one fitted method, a numeric matrix with parameters in rows and the lower and upper confidence limits in two percentage-labelled columns. For an object containing multiple fitted methods, a named list of such matrices, one per method. The result is returned visibly and contains only interval bounds.

add_confint()

A copy of the amerasfit object, returned invisibly, with a CI element added to each fitted method. Method-specific timing is updated to include interval computation. Each CI element contains lower and upper. Profile likelihood results additionally contain boundary p-values and iteration counts in pval.lower, pval.upper, iter.lower, and iter.upper.

Details

Both functions use the same interval calculations and always compute the requested intervals, even if object already contains attached intervals. The input object is left unchanged.

Use confint() when only standalone bounds are needed, for example for comparison or export. Use add_confint() when the fit will be retained for reporting or further inspection: summary() and coef(summary(object)) include the attached bounds, profile-likelihood diagnostics are stored when available, and computation time is recorded. Assign the invisibly returned object to retain this information. Any previously attached intervals are replaced in that returned copy. Use summary() to display the stored intervals and print(summary(fit), digits = 3), for example, to control the printed precision. Attaching intervals is particularly useful for expensive profile likelihood calculations because subsequent summaries use the stored results without repeating the calculation.

Interval types

For RC, ERC, and MCML, Wald intervals on the original parameter scale use the delta-method variance-covariance matrix. Wald intervals on the transformed scale are computed in the optimization parametrization and then back-transformed. More specifically, when \(\boldsymbol\theta = h(\boldsymbol\eta)\), transformed-scale intervals apply \(h\) to the endpoints on the \(\boldsymbol\eta\) scale, whereas original-scale intervals use the covariance matrix obtained from \(J H^{-1} J^T\), where \(J\) is the transformation Jacobian and \(H\) is the optimization Hessian. Transformed-scale intervals can therefore be asymmetric on the reported parameter scale. Profile likelihood intervals repeatedly re-evaluate the likelihood and can therefore be substantially more expensive.

For FMA and BMA, percentile intervals use equal-tailed sample quantiles and HPD intervals use HPDinterval.

Profile likelihood bracketing

Before determining bounds, a separate adaptive search first finds a bracket for each lower and upper bound. A bracket is an interval within which the likelihood-ratio p-value crosses the target 1 - level. The search proceeds outward from the fitted parameter value on the internal optimizer scale. Initial search distances are four approximate standard errors when the stored Hessian is usable; otherwise, fallback starting points are used. If necessary, the search distance is doubled up to 12 times. Each profile evaluation may require re-optimizing the nuisance parameters, so bracketing can itself be computationally expensive, particularly for ERC and MCML.

Once a bracket is found, uniroot locates the bound within it using tol.profCI and maxit.profCI. These arguments control root finding only; they do not affect the bracketing search. If a bound cannot be bracketed or reliably solved, it is returned as NA with a warning reporting the last attempted parameter value and its p-value. A bracketing failure can reflect a limited search range, parameter scaling, numerical problems in the profile evaluations, or the absence of a finite bound.

When a model was fitted with keep.data = FALSE, the original data must be supplied through data for profile likelihood intervals. The missing-value policy used during fitting is reapplied before likelihood evaluation. Wald and sample-based intervals do not require the original data. For models with formula effect modifiers, subgroup-specific profile intervals can be obtained by fitting subgroup-specific dose coefficients with modifier = ~ 0 + M or modifier = ~ M - 1.

See also

ameras for model fitting, summary for fit summaries, and confint for the generic function. See also vignette("confidenceintervals", package = "ameras").

Examples

fit <- ameras(
  Y.binomial ~ dose(V1:V3, model = "ERR"),
  data = ameras_simulated,
  family = "binomial",
  methods = "RC"
)
#> Fitting RC

## Compute standalone Wald bounds
confint(fit, type = "wald.orig")
#>                  2.5 %     97.5 %
#> (Intercept) -1.0297063 -0.7404073
#> dose         0.5338981  1.0748159

## Attach Wald intervals for use in summaries
fit_with_ci <- add_confint(fit, type = "wald.orig")
summary(fit_with_ci)
#> Call:
#> ameras(formula = Y.binomial ~ dose(V1:V3, model = "ERR"), data = ameras_simulated, 
#>     family = "binomial", methods = "RC")
#> 
#> Rows: 3000
#> 
#> Total CPU runtime: 0 seconds
#> 
#> CPU runtime in seconds by method:
#> 
#>  Method   Fit  CI Total
#>      RC 0.021 0.0 0.021
#> 
#> Summary of coefficients by method:
#> 
#>  Method        Term Estimate     SE CI.lower CI.upper
#>      RC (Intercept)  -0.8851 0.0738  -1.0297  -0.7404
#>      RC        dose   0.8044 0.1380   0.5339   1.0748
#> 

## Attach expensive profile intervals for subsequent reporting

fit_with_profile_ci <- add_confint(
  fit,
  type = "proflik",
  parm = "dose"
)
#> Obtaining profile likelihood CI for dose
summary(fit_with_profile_ci)
#> Call:
#> ameras(formula = Y.binomial ~ dose(V1:V3, model = "ERR"), data = ameras_simulated, 
#>     family = "binomial", methods = "RC")
#> 
#> Rows: 3000
#> 
#> Total CPU runtime: 0.1 seconds
#> 
#> CPU runtime in seconds by method:
#> 
#>  Method   Fit    CI Total
#>      RC 0.021 0.054 0.075
#> 
#> Summary of coefficients by method:
#> 
#>  Method        Term Estimate     SE CI.lower CI.upper
#>      RC (Intercept)  -0.8851 0.0738       NA       NA
#>      RC        dose   0.8044 0.1380   0.5661    1.114
#>
